children: Cryptocurrencies are broadly lower in Asia as markets eye U.S. midterms and implications for digital-asset regulation. A result that gives Democrats decisive control of Congress could spur a knee-jerk negative reaction on perceptions of tougher or slower crypto regulation. But concerns could be overdone. The most recent legislative setback for crypto--the failure of the Clarity Act procedural vote--didn't materially dent expectations of more institutional adoption and continued regulatory progress. Still, the macro backdrop remains delicate. Renewed escalation in the Middle East refreshes concerns about energy prices and inflation, pushing yields higher and pressuring risk assets, says Firas Bechwaty at ICM MENA. Coming U.S. economic data reinforcing rate-hike views or cautious guidance from AI-related companies could dim sentiment further. Bitcoin falls 0.8%; Ethereum drops 1.1%.(fabiana.negrinochoa@wsj.com)
